title: Open Google search results in a new tab
question: How do I make Google open search results in a new tab?
answer: Google has its own setting for this: Search settings > Other settings > "Results in a new window", available signed in or out, but it opens each result in a new window. The usermods script on this page makes every link in the Google results list open in a new tab instead, and keeps the results page open in the current tab. Install it with usermods or any userscript manager. Without a script, Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on a Mac) or middle-click a result.
prompt: Make Google search results open in a new tab.
details: The script sets `target="_blank"` on links in the results list that lead away from the results page, including Google's `/goto` and `/url` redirect links, and re-applies it as more results load. Tabs, the search box and links that stay on the results page (more results, related searches) open as before. The check clicks a result and confirms the results page stays put.

alternatives.title: Google's "Results in a new window" setting
alternatives.body: Open [Search settings](https://www.google.com/preferences), choose **Other settings** and turn on **Results in a new window**. It works signed out too. Results open in a new browser window rather than a tab.

alternatives.title: Ctrl-click or middle-click
alternatives.body: Hold **Ctrl** (**Cmd** on a Mac) while clicking a result, or click it with the middle mouse button.

evidence.note: Greasy Fork total installs: "Google-open-in-new-tab" (read via api.greasyfork.org, 2026-11-17)
suggests "how to make google always open search result links in new tabs"

check.actions: window.__usermodsStart = location.href; const first = [...document.querySelectorAll('#rso a[href]:has(h3)')].find((a) => a.checkVisibility()); if (first && first.target === '_blank') first.click();
check.expect: (() => { const l = [...document.querySelectorAll('#rso a[href]:has(h3)')].filter((a) => a.checkVisibility()); return location.href === window.__usermodsStart && l.length > 0 && l.every((a) => a.target === '_blank'); })()
